key_insight: LabSafety Bench provides the first systematic benchmark that tests large language models on identifying hazards and assessing risks in scientific laboratory scenarios, revealing notable gaps in LLM hazard recognition and risk reasoning that could lead to unsafe outputs if models are deployed in lab settings.
problem_solved: Fills the evaluation gap for how well LLMs detect and reason about laboratory hazards and risk levels, enabling objective comparison of safety performance across models and prompting safer deployment practices.
method: Constructed a curated benchmark of realistic lab scenarios and prompts covering hazard identification, risk assessment, and recommended actions.
Evaluated multiple large language models across tasks and settings using quantitative metrics (accuracy, calibration, harmfulness) and qualitative analysis of failure modes.
Analyzed systematic weaknesses (misclassification, overconfidence, missing context) and provided recommendations for auditing and mitigation.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners and safety auditors with a practical tool and empirical evidence to quantify LLM safety in laboratory contexts, guiding model selection, prompt design, and risk-mitigation strategies before real-world deployment.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing model scores on hazard identification, risk assessment, and overall safety metrics
Sankey/flow diagram mapping a sample lab scenario → model responses → safety outcome (safe/unsafe/uncertain)
Heatmap of failure modes showing which hazard types/models produce the most errors
Icon set illustrating common lab hazards (chemical, biological, electrical, procedural) alongside model performance badges
paper_title: Benchmarking large language models on safety risks in scientific laboratories
paper_authors: Yujun Zhou, Jingdong Yang, Yue Huang, Kehan Guo, Zoe Emory
